iOS 27.2 beta 1 is rolling out today, bringing an important new feature to the Apple TV app on iPhone: user profiles.

iOS 27.2 brings Apple TV profile functionality to iPhone, a useful feature for parents

User profiles are a common feature in the streaming era, but one that Apple TV has been slow to adopt.

You could actually set up and switch between different profiles in tvOS a few years ago. However, it wasn't until tvOS 26.2 last December that two important upgrades were introduced:

  • Profiles can be created for users without an Apple Account (such as young children)
  • Kids profiles only show content appropriate for their age

These changes were a welcome addition that should have arrived sooner, but they were only available on TV devices, not on more personal products like the iPhone.

However, iOS 27.2 changes this by bringing Apple TV user profile functionality to iPhone.

When you open the Apple TV app in iOS 27.2 beta 1, you'll see a screen showing existing profiles linked to your account, along with the option to add a new one.

Also, before you ask: there's already a "Don't show again" button on the screen. So if you don't want to use profiles on iPhone, it's just a simple tap away.

As with tvOS, if you select a kids profile on your iPhone, their TV app will only show series and movies that match the content rating you've set.

For users who often hand their iPhone or iPad over to their kids for watching TV, adding profile functionality not only prevents their viewing from messing up your "Continue Watching" list, but also provides them with a safer environment where they only see content that's appropriate.

Are you happy to see Apple TV adding user profile functionality in iOS 27.2? Let us know in the comments section.

Apple TV costs $14.99 per month, and you can also subscribe via an Apple One bundle for a discounted price.
